svg.text: Red triangles: the 99 annual peaks as published; blue: what the all-years curve gives at the same stage (bar: the curves whose zero-flow stage e is in its 95% interval). Dashed: the
highest stage ever measured, 36.25 ft; only 65 of 4117 measurements are at 30 ft or more. At the record stage (36.97 ft, 1993) the curve gives 565148 ft³/s against the published
750000 (-24.6%), and the curves whose e is in its 95% interval differ by only 3.4%: the statistics are far too confident. The real uncertainty is in the measurements themselves: the
12 measured at 34.5 ft or more range from 418000 to 750000 ft³/s (×1.79), because in a flood the stage also depends on whether the river is rising or falling, on backwater from
the Mississippi and on levees failing upstream. The historic peaks of 1844 and 1903 (estimated from flood marks) sit far from today's curve at their stage: the channel, levees and
gage datum were different. Hover a peak for its flags; click for the gage.
